extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental investigators, and researchers applying Baconian/empirical method
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assembling and using special classes of empirical 'instances' (examples/observations) to correct habit, delimit forms, and decide between competing causes in natural-philosophical investigation (Baconian method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviating instances (errors of nature / monstrous objects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deviating instances, such as the errors of nature or strange and monstrous objects in which nature deviates; the errors of nature differ from singular instances in that the latter are miracles of species, the former of individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to rectify understanding corrupted by habit: investigate until the cause of deviation is discerned (the latent process toward a form). They are especially useful for practical/operative inquiry because varying known species is often easier than generating new species. Compile a particular natural history of monsters and prodigies, but select rigorously and prefer grave, credible histories; be suspicious of accounts arising from superstition, natural magic, alchemy, or fabulists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bordering instances (participants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bordering instances (participants) exhibit bodies/species that appear composed of two species or act as rudiments between one and the other (i.e., intermediate forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class separately because they point out order, constitution, and suggest causes of number and quality of common species, leading understanding from what is to what is possible. Examples: moss (between putrescence and plant), some comets (between stars and meteors), flying fishes (between fishes and birds), bats (between birds and quadrupeds), biformed fœtus; treat as heteroclite or singular but considered for their explanatory dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of power (the wit or hands of man / masterpieces of art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of power are works most noble and perfect — masterpieces in every art — also termed the 'wit or hands of man' (fasces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit and examine all mechanical and practical liberal arts; compile a particular history of great masterpieces and modes of effecting them. These works facilitate invention and application (lead to new works more easily than chance). Caution: do not let magnificent works 'depress' or 'chain' the understanding into thinking nothing can be achieved without identical means. Also include singular instances of art (e.g., paper) and investigate charms/conjuring; investigate superstition/magic for any latent natural operations (e.g., fascination, sympathy) rather than dismissing outright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similar instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar instances (one of the 'last five species' named alongside singular, deviating, bordering, and power instances) — instances that are analogous or exhibit likenesses across domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with the rest of the five as a preparative collection to correct habitual understanding and ready the mind for operative deductions; gather them together as a particular history to arrange matter entering the understanding and to purify it from daily impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singular instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular instances (miracles of species) — unique or exceptional natural facts that stand out as singular examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Like similar and deviating instances, collect as part of the preparative history. Singular instances (e.g., the sun, moon, magnet) may be familiar yet singular in nature and useful both for elevating understanding and as objects of comparison for forms; do not reserve them only for one investigation but compile them collectively with the other special instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompanying and hostile instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Accompanying instances exhibit concretes where the required nature is constantly found as an inseparable companion; hostile instances show concretes where the required nature is constantly avoided and excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From these form certain and universal (or near-universal) affirmative or negative propositions about concretes and their predicates. Use accompanying instances to narrow the affirmative of form (the form must enter into the concretion), and hostile instances to establish what forms are repugnant. Note two important points: (1) if no universal affirmative/negative exists, record that fact; (2) append to general propositions the concretes approaching nearest the non-existing substance (limits) to circumscribe forms. Examples: flame accompanies heat; air is hostile to solidity. Universal exceptions need not be absolute if they are singular/rare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjunctive instances (instances of extremity or limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjunctive instances (instances of extremity or limits) indicate real divisions of nature and measures of things — showing 'how far' nature effects or allows anything and her passage to something else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to determine the extents and boundaries of qualities (both in abundance and defect). Examples: gold as an extreme in weight, iron in hardness, the whale in animal size, dog in smell, flame of gunpowder in rapid expansion; include extremes of defect such as spirits of wine in lightness or worms on skin in animal size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of alliance (union)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of alliance (union) are examples that mingle and unite natures held to be heterogeneous, showing that effects thought peculiar to one nature may be produced by another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to elevate the mind from perceived differences to genus and to reveal that differences may be modifications of a common nature. Investigate how allied instances reduce supposed essential differences by analyzing degree, quality, inequality, and temporality (e.g., sun's heat vs fire: milder degree, more moist quality, inequality, and gradual long-term operation). Examples include vine branches ripening near constant fire, reviving cold butterflies by gentle warmth, eggs hatched by fire-like heat, and low comets revolving like higher bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of the cross (decisive / judicial instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of the cross (decisive, judicial, oracle, command) are sought when the understanding is balanced between two or more candidate natures; they show which union with the required nature is firm and which is separable, thereby deciding the cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively seek or create these decisive instances to terminate interpretation and complete inquiry. They may be newly observed or already known. Use them to reject competing hypotheses by designing targeted observations or experiments (examples and suggested decisive experiments are given for tides, diurnal motion, gravity vs attraction, magnetic polarity, etc.). For instance, compare simultaneous tides across isthmuses, sound the sea to detect curvature in ebb/flood, observe motion in air/low comets/planets to judge diurnal motion, or use paired clocks (weight-driven vs spring) at different altitudes to test whether attraction varies with depth/height. The method emphasizes careful, purposeful empirical tests to decide between alternatives.
